messages:
alex: quick follow-up on the stalled-prefetch backoff idea i posted earlier — sketched a small proposal for a cooldown+coalesce heuristic to avoid noisy prefetch storms when resident sets are tight.

maria: can you paste the config sketch? curious how you'd tune cooldown vs coalesce window.

alex: sure — basic idea: track per-tenant prefetch stalls (prefetch requested but page already queued or IO in-flight). increment a stall counter, trigger exponential cooldown on subsequent prefetches for that tenant until stall counter decays. also batch coalesce windows when cooldown active to reduce tiny IOs.

alex: code sketch:
```
# config for prefetch backoff/coalesce
prefetch_backoff:
  base_cooldown_ms: 50
  max_cooldown_ms: 2000
  stall_threshold: 3
  decay_half_life_s: 30
coalesce:
  base_window_ms: 5
  max_window_ms: 100
  expand_factor_on_cooldown: 4
```

tj: makes sense. sequence length / request concurrency will affect these numbers a lot. did you simulate on 1k qps with bursty tails?

alex: i ran a small local sim — workload with frequent KV cache misses + 10–20 request concurrency per tenant. result: p50 unchanged, p95 ~ +1–2ms, p99 improved by ~6% vs always-prefetch strategy (we avoid dozens of 1–2ms IOs at the tail).

sam: interesting. how does this interact with our KV cache and existing auto-batcher? if we coalesce in software we may duplicate work with hardware-level batching.

alex: good point. plan is to expose a hint to the runtime's batcher: when tenant is in cooldown, the prefetch hint becomes "defer" and the batcher treats it as low priority and tries to coalesce into the next batch window. if the hardware/GPU runtime already coalesces, the hint is a no-op.

maria: any concerns with fairness? a noisy tenant might get stuck in cooldown and starve others if their demotions are aggressive.

alex: fairness handled two ways: 1) cooldown is tenant-scoped only (we don't global-suppress prefetch for the whole host), 2) cooldown uses decay so a single recovery request quickly reduces stall counter. also we limit max cooldown to avoid indefinitely delaying critical inf requests.

natalie: what about fragmented pages — coalesce window may pull adjacent pages and increase fragmentation churn if we do lots of small compactions after.

alex: coalesce is read-side only (we're coalescing prefetch IOs). write-path compaction would be unchanged. but i added a guard: if host fragmentation metric (prometheus: host_fragmentation_ratio) > 0.6, reduce expand_factor_on_cooldown to 1 to avoid large fanouts.

sam: could we expose a per-tenant opt-out? some latency-sensitive customers may prefer always-prefetch.

alex: yes — expose policy: prefetch_policy = [always, cooldown-aware, disabled]. default cooldown-aware.

infra-bot: ci/build #5621 passed — diff includes prefetch backoff config + unit tests.

tj: test plan? need e2e with a mixed-tenant slow-storage case (simulate NVMe saturations) and a microbench for p99 change.

alex: test plan in PR: unit tests for stall counter decay + integration that replays a trace with bursts (script included). e2e: run small cluster with fio-backed slow tier and synthetic clients to measure tail.

maria: can you add a telemetry tag to the cooldown events? we want a counter and histogram of cooldown durations per-tenant so we can tune in prod.

alex: will add: metric pref.backoff.cooldown_count{tenant,reason}, and pref.backoff.duration_ms histogram. also a debug log at info when tenant crosses stall_threshold.

natalie: one last thing — make sure rollout plan includes a canary with dedicated pool so we can observe cross-tenant effects before global rollout.

alex: agreed. canary plan: 5% of traffic on dedicated pool, monitor p99, IO ops/sec, host_fragmentation_ratio, and pref.backoff.* metrics for 6h. rollback if p99 degrades >5% or fragmentation increases >10%.

sam: :thumbsup: if we keep the default conservative and have solid telemetry this seems low-risk.

alex: i'll open the PR with the config + tests + telemetry and tag you all. thanks for quick feedback.

maria: thanks — quick nit: call the config field prefetch_cooldown instead of prefetch_backoff to avoid confusion with network-level backoff.

alex: noted, will rename in PR.

infra-bot: deploy-preview created: https://ci.redwood/preview/5621

sam: cool — feel free to @me on the PR if you want pairing for the e2e script.

alex: will do.
